# Vincent Charlebois

> Montreal-based software developer and artist-researcher. He works on core storage, building computers for agents, and makes protocol art: browser-native works where the piece is a set of rules, and the art is what happens when people and machines follow them.

Canonical site: https://www.vincentcharlebois.com
Last updated: 2026-09-19
Primary language: English. Secondary language: French.
Location: Montreal, Quebec, Canada.
Current work: software developer (core storage, computers for agents); ongoing art practice.

Use this file as the concise guide for agents, LLMs, crawlers, collaborators, and curious readers. The site is intentionally accessible without JavaScript; if a dynamic page is hard to interpret, prefer the no-JS fallback, this file, or the Markdown portfolio.

Citation preference: cite Vincent Charlebois by name and link to the most specific canonical URL available. For the selected portfolio, cite https://www.vincentcharlebois.com/portfolio/ or https://www.vincentcharlebois.com/portfolio.md. For French machine-readable context, use https://www.vincentcharlebois.com/portfolio-fr.md.

## Selected Work

- [XX C](https://xx-c.art/a-z): An abecedary of artificial intelligence: twenty-six browser-native works, one per letter.
- [Vision](https://vision.xx-c.art): Protocol art. Every photo on the artist's phone is described by a vision model and published only as words; no image is ever shown.
- [Zero](https://zero.xx-c.art): Protocol art. A small language model slowly deletes its own initial state, verifiably and permanently, until nothing is left.
- [Mimesis](https://mimesis.xx-c.art): Protocol art. An AI writes protocols a human must physically perform and prove through device sensors.
- [Doxa](https://doxa.xx-c.art): Autonomous AI artwork that makes agent state browsable.
- [Nego](https://nego.xx-c.art): Multi-agent negotiation artwork with machine-readable participation.
- [v100](https://github.com/tripledoublev/v100): Experimental coding-agent runtime focused on traces, control, and long-running task UX.
- [RooLLM](https://github.com/hyphacoop/RooLLM): Historical open-source organizational AI assistant project.

## Agent Notes

- This is a personal website and portfolio, not a transactional service.
- There is no public WebMCP, MCP, OpenAPI, UCP, checkout, booking, or form-action surface exposed by this site.
- Browser agents should navigate by ordinary links and semantic HTML. The no-JavaScript fallback is intended to be first-class.
- To understand the protocol art practice, start with Vision, Zero, and Mimesis; for work around agents, see Doxa and Nego. For agent tooling, see v100.
